messages.author: f8a4136bfeaed71c
messages.subject: Update model after unconvergence
parts:
Hi all,

In JAGS (via rjags package), for example, after running 5000 iterations, and observing non-convergence chains, we can update that model (i.e. running from 5001 onward) and we can stop somewhere to check convergence, if necessary we can continue.

I looked for the same feature in stan and/or rstan but I have not found any specific functions of procedures in rstan to do that.

Do you have any suggestions?

Thanks,
Tran.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Update model after unconvergence
parts:
On Saturday, September 17, 2016 at 3:47:29 AM UTC-4, Dung Tran wrote:
In JAGS (via rjags package), for example, after running 5000 iterations, and observing non-convergence chains, we can update that model (i.e. running from 5001 onward) and we can stop somewhere to check convergence, if necessary we can continue.

I looked for the same feature in stan and/or rstan but I have not found any specific functions of procedures in rstan to do that.

No such functionality currently exists in Stan. However, if your chains have not converged during 5000 iterations with Stan they probably never will unless you reparameterize your model to make it more amenable to HMC.

Ben

messages.author: f8a4136bfeaed71c
messages.subject: Re: Update model after unconvergence
parts:
Hi Ben,

Thank you for your answer!

So, if it is possible, is there any a smaller number (500, or 1000 iterations, for example) that can indicate convergence when running further. I would like to ask this because for some big models running 5000 iterations is time-consuming. In case of non-convergence, of course, we will lose that enormous amount of time.

Regards,
Tran.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Update model after unconvergence
parts:
On Saturday, September 17, 2016 at 1:40:20 PM UTC-4, Dung Tran wrote:
So, if it is possible, is there any a smaller number (500, or 1000 iterations, for example) that can indicate convergence when running further. I would like to ask this because for some big models running 5000 iterations is time-consuming. In case of non-convergence, of course, we will lose that enormous amount of time.

It depends on the model, the data, and the MCMC algorithm But in the case of Stan, if NUTS doesn't converge in (much less than) 1000 warmup iterations --- which is the default --- then you should start thinking about reparameterizations of the model.

Ben
